A crown of vertebrae turns toward you. The throne room exhales dust.
A mountain of ice with something furious frozen at its centre.
ALL OF IT COMES BACK TOGETHER.
Break the shell. I dare you.
CEILING SUPPORT COMPROMISED. THIS IS INTENTIONAL.
CLOSE YOUR EYES. IT WILL NOT HELP.
Cold enough to forget your own name.
DOWN. ALL OF IT GOES DOWN.
EVERY MOUTH IN THIS PLACE IS SCREAMING MY NAME.
Every book in this hall is a name. He has been waiting to add yours.
Every corpse in this floor is an egg.
Everything I have eaten is still screaming. Join the chorus.
Everything that ever went missing down here is in there, and still awake.
Everything that falls in here is added to me. Come and be added.
Fine. I will do it myself.
Footnotes. Everywhere. Read them or die ignorant.
For every one you kill I make three.
Full plate, no visor slit. Whatever is inside does not need to see.
GEOMETRY IS A COURTESY. I WITHDRAW IT.
Ground yourself. It will not be enough.
HOLD STILL. THIS IS DELICATE WORK.
He has been preaching to an empty waste for years. You are the first congregation.
He is mostly other people. They are all still moving.
Hold still. I am recording this.
Hold the line. I always do.
I AM NO LONGER A MAN. I AM A CONCLUSION.
I HAVE BEEN COLD FOR A THOUSAND YEARS.
I HAVE NEVER LOST. I WILL NOT LEARN TODAY.
I SEE IT NOW. SO WILL YOU.
I will give some of them back. You will not enjoy it.
IT IS COMING. I AM ONLY THE NOTICE.
It does not have a front. Wherever you stand, you are being looked at.
It has eaten everything else in this chamber. The armour is still visible inside it.
It is announcing something. The announcement is happening inside your skull.
It was here before you opened the door. It has been here the whole time.
LOOK UP. THAT IS NOT THE CEILING.
Listen. It is the last kindness I have.
My court is endless. Cut them down and you will only tire.
My flock will hold you while I finish.
My guard will not tire. You will.
My hands are many. Break them all.
My phylactery walks among the dead. Find it.
My pylons will do the arithmetic.
My retinue first. I am not finished with my drink.
PURGE CYCLE ENGAGED. VACATE THE FLOOR.
Roots have found every corpse in this temple and put them all to work.
Rot is only a root that has learned to be hungry.
STRIKE THE CRUST BEFORE IT HARDENS.
She does not fight you. She lets the pack do that, and watches.
Six centuries of standing perfectly still end in a single grinding step.
Six seals are already broken. He is very close to whatever he wanted.
Stand still and I will make you a monument.
Steel is honest. You are not.
THE DEEP FIRE HAS A KING.
THE HIVE IS ONE. THE HIVE IS ME.
THEN I WILL BURY US BOTH.
THEN THE WHOLE MOUNTAIN COMES DOWN.
THERE IS NOTHING BELOW ME. THERE IS NOTHING ABOVE YOU.
The air tastes of copper. Your hair is standing up and it is not fear.
The floor is tacky underfoot. Something enormous drags a hook across stone.
The great hammer has not stopped falling in four hundred years. It stops now.
The grove does not forgive axes.
The hive is not her home. The hive is her body, and you are inside it.
The lava is not a hazard in this room. The lava is him, and he is standing up.
The mass does not die. It divides.
The water in this temple has been waiting a long time to be told what to do.
The webs are not decoration. They are a nervous system, and it just felt you.
Then I will come down to you.
There is nothing below this floor. He is what the bottom looks like.
Which of us is the original? Guess.
Which one is real? Neither answer saves you.
You are already breathing me in.
You are late. The work is nearly done.
You came a long way down to die somewhere memorable.
You cannot outrun what does not tire.
You mistook it for architecture for a full minute. It let you.
You were never the hunter here.
You will break on my shield before I break on your sword.
You will not see the end coming.

A CRACK. A CRACK IN THE GLAZE.
A bog queen rises from the peat, green lanterns glowing round her like a court. Each lantern beats like a heart.
A boiler on legs stands in a cloud of its own steam. Gauges on its chest tick toward red. The valves on its back are within reach.
A ceramic giant glazed in blue and gold sheds water as it walks. Where the water pools, the floor hisses. Its glaze has never cracked.
A clockwork priest the size of a chapel door turns its face, a clock face, toward you. All its hands point to the same hour.
A crook taps on frozen stone. Sheep made of candle wax pour out of glowing doors, and every one of them walks to the shepherd and melts into his cloak.
A goblin in a crown of bent spoons rides an iron shield down the slope like a sled, whooping. His court cheers from the gutters.
A king in a crown of gold, and over it a crown of thorns, kneels before an empty altar. Around him lie the weapons of every war he won.
A lady in a drowned ballgown salutes you with a rapier. "First blood, or last?" she asks, and does not wait for an answer.
A stair that fell a thousand years ago got up again. It wears its own steps as armour, and its knees are landings.
A whale in a coat of gold coins hangs in the flooded nave. Every tithe the temple ever took is nailed to its hide.
A woman with a chain and a brass level walks the floor, marking tiles in chalk. "Hold this end," she says. "Do not step out of the measure."
An old woman made of packed snow sits by a cold hearth, knitting with icicles. "Come closer, dear," she says. "It is so warm with you here."
And last, with nothing in my hands at all.
Another room. Another wall of wings.
Ash falls like snow. Footprints walk across it toward you, and there is nobody making them.
Break them all you like. Hearts grow back, here.
Buy ash? Everyone is buying ash, this year.
Catch me, and the crows are yours. Nobody catches me.
Come in. Every door here is open to you. Once.
Count them in. One. Two. Always one more.
Crows line every branch, every beam, every inch of the walls. A man in a feather cloak bows, and they all lift at once.
Do not touch the bells. They are not yours to ring.
Down the stair, again. I have always been one room ahead.
Eight forms you have seen. Nobody sees the ninth twice.
Every break makes more of you. I have all the glass I need.
Every layer chained me. Every layer broke.
Every wall of the hall is a door, and every door is ajar. A tall figure steps out of one, and back into another, and is behind you.
Four chains as thick as a man run from four anchors to one huge throat. It strains at them. The anchors groan. The walls are already cracked.
Hold still. I am taking your measure.
Hush now. Mother is here. Mother is everywhere.
I WAS FIRED IN THE HOTTEST KILN. NOTHING YOU CARRY WILL MARK ME.
I know this one. You always open with this one.
I was crowned for the sword. Let us begin there.
IT IS THE HOUR. IT IS ALWAYS THE HOUR.
If you fall, I lift you. And I you, brother.
Keep your little light. It is the last one. I want to watch it go out.
LAST HOUR. NO MORE HOURS AFTER THIS.
LOUDER, THE BOTH OF US. LET THE BELLOWS HEAR.
Louder. LOUDER. The rafters must hear.
Make way! MAKE WAY for the KING!
Mind your feet. I set those for something bigger.
No more rooms. Then it is you, me, and all of them.
Nobody said fair. I never said fair!
Now they close. All but mine.
Oh, now you have done it. Out, my lovelies, OUT!
Oh. Oh, you are too warm. Look what you are doing to me.
One. Two. Three. Walk where I mark, and only there.
Orrin. Company. I see them, Ebb.
PRESSURE CRITICAL. STAND CLEAR. STAND CLEAR.
Panes of glass stand all over the hall, each one framed in lead. In every one of them you can see yourself, and in one of them you are smiling.
Put out the light, and there will be nothing left to read.
Shelves without end, and all the books are blank. One lantern burns on a lectern. A long grey shape is erasing the room around it, line by line.
Sing with us. Everyone sings, in the end.
Sit. Sit. You will catch your death, standing.
Small and quick, like I was as a girl.
Snares hang from every hook in the room. A woman in a leather apron counts them under her breath, and the sack on her back squirms.
Somebody had to come up. It was going to be one of us.
Someone is waiting at the bottom of the stair. They have your coat, your stance, your weapon. They look up, and they have your face, and they are a little sorry about it.
Strike when I am open. If you can tell.
THE HOUR TURNS BACK. I TURN WITH IT.
The One Who Came Up Instead
The black pools in the floor are not puddles. One of them breathes. Salt crusts the walls in the shape of a long, long body.
The dark here is thick as wax. Somewhere in it a woman hums a lullaby, and small feet patter from brazier to brazier, putting them out.
The deep is not square. I will make it square.
The floor heaves. Something the size of a cart is rooting under it, snorting, and it has smelled you.
The hour is called. Kneel, or be counted.
Then fire, for the heretics. I was crowned twice for that.
Then the bow, for those who ran.
Then the mace, for the rebels.
There is no floor below this one. Something here has your name in its mouth, and every name before yours, and it is tired of saying them.
They buried me. The bog would not keep me.
Three bells hang dark over a drowned chapel. A nun with a hand-bell waits at the altar. When she sees you, she starts to toll.
Three corpses stand in a choir stall, still singing. The lowest voice is the loudest. The highest one never stops.
Three furnaces stand in a row, and they are singing. The fire sings high. The slag answers low. Smoke hums the space between.
Two pale brothers stand back to back in the reeds. One holds a cleaver, one a dripping staff. They speak in turns, and never finish a sentence for each other.
You came all this way. Let me remember you properly.
You found me. Now find me again.
You lit my candles. Now you will burn down with them.
You scattered my flock. I will have your fleece for it.
A company of the dead stands in ranks, still in delver's gear, still at attention. At its head a marshal reads the roll by a cold blue light. He reaches the end and looks up. Your name is not on it.
A door stands in the middle of the room with no wall around it. It opens. Something very tall and very polite unfolds through it, bowing, and the room behind you is no longer the room you came in by.
A long table set for a hundred. Every candle is lit and every chair is empty. At its head a woman of old wax rises from her seat, and the whole house rises with her.
Bows! Show them how we held the forty-first.
Crack me, then. Every crack is one more edge.
Every pane in its place. Step where the light says, or be cut to fit.
Fall in, delver. Name and company. You are forty years late.
Forgive me. I am moving the floor. You were standing on it.
Give me that lamp, dear. Nobody reads in this house after dark.
Hold still. I almost have you. I almost always have you.
Hold still. You are the wrong shape for the window.
I have made you a hall with no end. Do walk it. It is the polite thing.
I sent them home every night, in my head. Not one of them went.
IF I LET GO, IT RISES. IF IT RISES, YOU ALL RISE WITH IT.
Mm. Another little light. Come closer. I am only dreaming you.
Nobody goes up until the roll is called. Nobody.
Panes of glass stand in rows across the room, each one cut to the shape of somebody. A tall figure of leaded glass is cutting another. It holds the blade up to you, and measures.
Shoes off at the door. Hands where I can see them.
THE BOLTS ARE GIVING. STAND ASIDE, SMALL ONE. OR HOLD WITH ME.
The floor here is warm, and it rises and falls, very slowly. Then it opens: a hand as big as a tower comes up through the stone, the way a sleeper reaches for something in a dream. It has found you.

The floor is one great iron plate, and something the size of a house is bolted to it. It has been holding the Spire down since before the first stair was cut. Above you, the stone groans upward a finger's width.
Then I must show you out. The Tenant is not receiving.
There are doors in my palm. Every one of them is a way down.
This way, please. Mind the step. There are a great many steps.
Up, all of you. Up! We have a guest, and the guest is making a mess.
When I close my hand, I wake. When I wake, there is no more down.
Blocks stored as bonus damage. Your next blow spends all of it. The count is the stored percent.
Fighting under your standard: more defense and damage while you stand inside its ring.
Guard set: more block chance and damage reduction.
Planted and holding: more defense and damage reduction, slower feet. Press Guard Stance again to drop it.
Rooted to the floor. Much more defense, block and damage reduction, and nothing can stun, hold or knock you back.
A blow that rings twice. 170% weapon damage (+22% per rank), then half a second later the helm rings again for half as much and the enemy is Rung for 0.6s.
A blow you block is answered. 12% chance (+1.5% per rank) on a block to strike back for 140% weapon damage.
A long, slow blow that spends every Dent on the enemy. 300% weapon damage (+42% per rank), and +30% more for each Dent it beats flat.
A short, exact thrust at one enemy for 120% weapon damage (+16% per rank). It is Opened: the wound bleeds for 5s, deeper with every cut, up to five. Needs a sword.
A vigil kept at a run. While it burns: +8% attack and cast speed (+1.2% per rank) and +6% movement speed (+0.8% per rank). One vigil at a time.
A vigil kept kneeling on iron. While it burns: +30% defense (+5% per rank) and +4% damage reduction (+0.6% per rank). Press again to put it out. One vigil at a time.
A vigil read from a burning writ. Enemies in the ring lose 8 of every resistance (+1 per rank). One vigil at a time.
A vigil round a charred rood. Everything in the ring takes 28% weapon damage (+4.5% per rank) as fire twice a second. One vigil at a time.
A vigil that makes the floor holy. Enemies in the ring are Consecrated: -20% movement speed (-1.5% per rank) and -5% attack speed (-0.5% per rank). One vigil at a time.
A vigil with a bell in it. Every 3 seconds it tolls: 120% weapon damage (+18% per rank) to everything in the ring, and each one is Rung for 0.3s (+0.02s per rank). One vigil at a time.
A vigil wrapped in thick censer smoke. Enemies in the ring Choke: -15 attack rating (-1.5 per rank) and -8% attack speed (-0.8% per rank). One vigil at a time.
Blade up and turned for 1.2s: +50% block chance. Then the answer, at the nearest enemy in front: 200% weapon damage (+25% per rank), and it is Exposed for 3s. Needs a sword.

Both hands on the haft and straight down, like a smith on cold iron. 220% weapon damage (+30% per rank) to one enemy and two Dents in its armour for 6s: each Dent is -12% defense and -4% physical resistance.
Burned once and never out. +2% fire resistance per rank (toward 30%), +8 life per rank, and every enemy that dies inside your vigil gives back 1% of your life (+0.3% per rank).
Call down the great bell on one enemy up to 12 metres off. It falls for 0.7s, then lands for 600% weapon damage (+85% per rank), and the enemy is Rung for 1.5s.
Capstone. Each critical rite Opens the enemy (one more stack every sixth rank), Opened enemies take 15% more damage from you (+2% per rank), and your bleeds tick 20% faster.
Capstone. Every fourth Mace blow is a Toll: +60% damage (+4% per rank), and the enemy is Rung for 0.8s.
Capstone. Two vigils burn at once, and every vigil is 10% stronger (+2% per rank).
Every blow is a confession beaten out of it. Your physical hits have a 10% chance (+1% per rank) to Dent the enemy for 6s.
Five cuts like five lines of a prayer, 50% weapon damage each (+7% per rank), every one Opening the same wound. Needs a sword.
Iron quenched in chapel water. +5% damage and +8 defense per rank.
Judgement, in one blow. 500% weapon damage (+70% per rank) to one enemy. It is Rung for 0.4s, and 0.4s longer for each Dent in its armour, up to 2.5s.
Kept sharp on the chapel step. +5% critical damage per rank and +1% life steal per rank (toward 8%).
Light a vigil of tallow candles at your feet. While it burns: +4 life (+1.5 per rank) and +1.5 mana (+0.3 per rank) back every second. Press again to put it out. One vigil at a time.
Like dropping a church step on it. +2 minimum and +3 maximum damage, and +3% critical damage, per rank.
Lunge up to 5 metres into one enemy for 260% weapon damage (+36% per rank). Every Opened cut on it confesses at once: +40% damage for each, and the wounds close. Needs a sword.
Maces and scepters. One target, hit until it stops: stagger it, dent it, ring it like a bell.
Name one enemy up to 14 metres off and condemn it. For 8s (+0.4s per rank): -20 attack rating (-2 per rank) and -15% defense (-2% per rank). If it dies censured, the censure finds the nearest enemy.
Never a wasted foot. +2% attack speed (toward 20%) and +1% movement speed (toward 12%) per rank.
Oil on the brow and on the weapon. For 20s (+1s per rank): +20% damage (+3% per rank) and +30 attack rating (+6 per rank).
One aura at a time, a ring of candle smoke at your feet. Vows for you, censures for them.
One heavy overhand blow at one enemy for 150% weapon damage (+18% per rank). It is Staggered for 2s: slower to move and to swing.
Prayers hammered into the plate. +14 defense and +1.5% damage reduction per rank.
Set the shield and lean in. For 5s (+0.15s per rank): +20% block chance and +10% damage reduction (+0.5% each per rank). Needs a shield.
Seven thrusts faster than the eye, 45% weapon damage each (+6.5% per rank). The seventh Exposes it and Opens it twice. Needs a sword.
Shield first, at one enemy up to 9 metres off. 140% weapon damage (+20% per rank), a hard shove, and it is Staggered for 2s. Needs a shield.
Show the blade one way, step to its side, and cut. 140% weapon damage (+20% per rank) to one enemy, and it is Exposed for 4s (+0.1s per rank): -20% defense, -8% physical resistance. Needs a sword.
Step round behind one enemy and put the blade through it: 450% weapon damage (+65% per rank). It is Opened three times and Exposed for 6s. Needs a sword.
Strike with the reliquary set in the shield boss. 140% weapon damage (+18% per rank); it spends every Dent on the enemy, and each one heals you 3% of your life (+0.15% per rank). Needs a shield.
Sung low, over the bleeding. +6% damage per rank against an enemy that is bleeding or Opened.
Swear to take the blows. For 10s (+0.3s per rank) a ward of 15% of your life (+2% per rank) soaks damage, and you take 5 less from each hit (+0.5 per rank).
Swing the censer out on its chain at one enemy up to 14 metres off. 160% weapon damage (+20% per rank) as fire, and it is Smoked for 4s: -30% attack rating while hot ash burns it.
Swords. Quick, exact cuts on one target: open it, answer it, finish it.
The bell cracked; it still rings. +12 life, +1.5 life regeneration and +1% physical resistance per rank (toward 25%).
The candles set further out. Your vigils reach 8% further per rank.
The evening office, said under every vigil. While one burns: +2 life per second and +1% damage reduction per rank.
The floor inside the ring makes them kneel. Enemies in any of your vigils are Penitent: -2% physical and fire resistance per rank.
The forms said over and over until the hand knows them. +2% critical chance per rank (toward 15%) and +12 attack rating per rank.
The hours kept, every one. +8 mana and +0.5 mana per second per rank, and +1% cast speed per rank (toward 15%).
The kind cut. 220% weapon damage (+30% per rank) to one enemy; one below 15% of its life (+0.5% per rank) takes eight times that. Never a boss. Needs a sword.
The long arm of a patient man. +1% critical chance per rank (toward 10%), +18 attack rating and +2 dexterity per rank.
The shield rim, edge-on, into one jaw. 80% weapon damage (+12% per rank), a short shove, and it is Rung for 1s (+0.03s per rank): stunned. Needs a shield.
The shield takes the blow and rings with it. +3% block chance per rank (toward 20%), and whatever you block is Staggered for 1.5s.
The verse no one forgets. Every fifth blow is a critical strike, and it lands 20% harder (+3% per rank).
Two cuts that cross on one enemy, 130% weapon damage each (+18% per rank). The second leaves it Exposed for 5s. Needs a sword.
Two quick cuts at one enemy, 90% weapon damage each (+12% per rank). Each one Opens it a little deeper. Needs a sword.
What is already broken breaks easier. +7% damage per rank against an enemy that is Staggered, Rung or Dented.
One target. One aura. No retreat.
Paladins fight with a mace or a sword, and a shield or both hands on the haft.

They rang the chapel bell until the rope burned through, then carried the clapper down the stair to ring it by hand. A Paladin brings iron, a shield scorched with old prayers, and one aura at a time: a ring of candle smoke at his feet that the dark does not cross cheaply. He picks one thing in the room and hits it until it stops.
Armour beaten out of shape. -12% defense and -4% physical resistance per dent, up to five.
Blade up and turned. +50% block chance until the answer comes.
Censer smoke in the throat. Less attack rating and slower attacks.
Cut along the grain and left to run. Physical damage over time, up to five cuts deep.
Eyes full of censer smoke and hot ash. -30% attack rating, and the coals keep burning.
Guard turned aside, armour gapped. -20% defense and -8% physical resistance.
Holy ground under unholy feet. Slower to move and to strike.
Inside the ring of candles. Life and mana come back faster.
Kept awake on the cold floor. More defense and damage reduction.
Kneeling in the ring whether it likes it or not. Lower physical and fire resistance.
Knocked off its feet by weight. -25% movement speed and -20% attack speed.
Named and condemned. Weaker blows, a thinner guard. When it dies the censure finds the next one.
Oil on the brow and the blade. More damage and attack rating.
Read out over it, and the words burn. Every resistance lowered.
Shield set against the door. +20% block chance and +10% damage reduction.
Struck like a bell, the skull still humming. Cannot act or move.
Sworn to take it. A ward of life soaks damage, and what gets through is less.
The blood up, the prayer fast. Faster attacks, casts and feet.
The evening office said under a vigil. More life regeneration and damage reduction.
+1 dexterity per rank. In cat form, also +2% attack speed and +1% movement speed per rank.
+1 life regeneration per rank. In bear form, also +1% damage reduction per rank (up to +20%).
+1 minimum and +2 maximum damage per rank.
+1% attack speed per rank. Pack Frenzy holds 1 more stack every 4 ranks.
+15 defense per rank and up to +20% physical resistance.
+2 life regeneration and +1 vitality per rank.
+2 vitality per rank. In bear form, also +2.5% life per rank (up to +60%).
+2 vitality per rank. In wolf form, also +14 defense per rank.
+3% damage per rank against any enemy carrying a debuff you put on it.
+6% damage per rank. In wolf form, also +25 attack rating per rank.
A bleeding thing is a slow thing. +5% damage per rank against Bleeding enemies.
A blow that would kill you leaves you on your feet with 30% life (+1% per rank) and 1.5s of untouchable grace. Once every 120s (4s less per rank, never under 60s).
A fast bite: 90% weapon damage (+13% per rank). Each Snap adds a stack of Pack Frenzy for 6s, +4% attack speed and +4% damage a stack, up to 5.
A low swipe at the back of the legs: 110% weapon damage (+16% per rank). The enemy is Crippled for 4s and Bleeds 2 stacks.
A low, wet howl. Heals you and your wolves 10% of life at once (+0.5% per rank), and for 8s every hit steals +6% life (+0.4% per rank).
A wide swipe that takes everything in front of you: 100% weapon damage (+15% per rank).

Become the bear: +30% life (+2% per rank), +40% defense (+6% per rank) and +6% damage reduction (+0.4% per rank), but 8% slower. Claw skills are fought in this form. Use it again to stand up as a man.

Become the great black cat: +12% movement speed (+1% per rank), +10% attack speed (+1% per rank) and +4% critical chance (+0.4% per rank). Feral skills are fought in this form. Use it again to stand up as a man.
Become the grey wolf: +20% damage (+3% per rank), +3% life steal (+0.2% per rank) and +40 attack rating (+15 per rank). Teeth skills are fought in this form. Use it again to stand up as a man.
Below 35% life you take 4% less damage per rank.
Below 35% life, +1.5% of every hit returns as life per rank.
Both paws up and down on the floor ahead: 160% weapon damage (+24% per rank) to everything within 3.2m of where they land, and knocks it down for 0.8s.
Charge up to 8m on all fours and run them down: 120% weapon damage (+18% per rank) to everything in your path, thrown 3m aside.
Circle one enemy and strike from every side: 6 blows (+1 every 5 ranks), each 45% weapon damage (+6% per rank), each one faster than the last.
Clamp on and shake. The enemy is held (stunned) while you shake it 4 times, each 40% weapon damage (+6% per rank), then thrown aside.
Clamp the jaws on one throat and wrench: 160% weapon damage (+24% per rank). Under 30% life it deals 2.5 times as much and leaves a Hemorrhage for 5s.
Drop low and go quiet for 4s: +30% movement speed (+1.5% per rank) and +20% critical chance (+0.5% per rank). Your next Feral skill deals +60% damage (+8% per rank) and ends it.
Drop low and spring up at the throat from up to 4m: 220% weapon damage (+30% per rank). Leaves a Hemorrhage for 6s and the enemy Weakened for 4s.
Each kill heals 1% of your life (+0.2% per rank). In cat form, +6% damage per rank.
Every 400 life you have adds +1% damage (+0.2% per rank).
Every hit you land adds +2% attack speed (+0.3% per rank) for a few seconds, stacking 5 times.
Grow into the great bear of the old stories for 12s (+0.5s per rank): bigger still, +30% life (+1.5% per rank), +30% damage (+2% per rank), and your swipes reach 40% further.
Hitting you hurts. 8% of every melee hit you take (+3% per rank) goes back to the attacker.

The fevered dream of green lanterns over black water.

The night ours rang, the Listener heard a second bell answer it. Far down, and under water.
The note on the Burning Steppe is three voices, a choir, practising.
The old survey puts a market square where the Bleached Reach has only dunes.
The oldest is the first thing that ever ate down here. Everything that went missing is inside it, still awake. I can hear them. Let them out.
The only order the Works ever finished is still waiting for its army.
The order was revised. You saw it. Someone changed it, in a hand that is not a clerk's, to something larger.
The rest of them are under seal. The Listener hears them in the crypt, very deep, behind seven doors and a thing that has been breaking the doors one at a time.
The rite also says to come back and put the lantern out. Nobody did. I was the one who was meant to.

The sick walk in their sleep, always toward the stair. When I hold them back, they talk about lanterns. Green ones, low over the water.

There. A nine hundred year debt, and it burns like any other paper.

Your pack smells like a ditch, which Vell will take as good news.

Cold, and full of a weather you cannot see.

My master learned from a woman who learned from a man, and so on back, a dozen pairs of hands, to someone who learned at Cindergate before the fall.

Nothing has ever come up into it. I would know. I sleep in it.

One of ours below at all times, and it stays below us. Three founders signed it. One of them went down to make sure.
Ordrun Kale. I mend what you break and I break what you cannot mend. Put it on the bench.
Pain is information. Numbing it is a decision, not a cure.
Past the bottom and still buying. My supplier will not believe it. I am my supplier.

Quiet. All the way down. I can hear you breathing, and under you, nothing. Nothing at all. I think I will sleep tonight.
Quiet. There. It heard you arrive. It always hears the new ones.
Report anything that comes up the stair. Anything.

Small blades. Fine work. I do not trust either, and I sharpen both.

Stone from the city's own foundations, laid dry, no mortar, by people who knew what mortar can be persuaded to do.

The city before the camp. It sold the deep its dead and kept the change. Nine hundred years of trade, and they still went under.

The dark down there is not the absence of light. It has a grain to it, like wood.

The fifth to hold the post, and the first to admit the maps are wrong. She measures everything twice, writes both numbers down, and is delighted when they disagree.
The front page of my pharmacopoeia. Nineteen people I could not bring back. I write the name, the tier, and what I did wrong.
The notation Caul used for depth. Very precise, very old. It has no word for bottom.

The wall has more names than the camp has people. The stonework has been extended twice.
There is a name in my wall I did not cut. I would know my own work. Somebody down there is doing the lettering now.
There is a sound under everything, very low, like a nail being worked loose by a patient hand. I hear it in my teeth now.
There is always a name in the down column. The council has never once allowed it to be empty. I used to wonder why that mattered so much to them.
There they are. Up the stair on their own feet. Somebody buy them a drink. Not me.
Things grow down there that ought to need sun. The grey mould from the crypt tiers cures fevers. I would like to know who is tending it.
Think about that the next time you pick up something they made, and like the balance.
Three came back. Two of those came back short of something you cannot see. I am the third. I came back with everything, and that is the worst of the three.

Twice in my service. Both times at night. Both times the gate watch swore nothing moved.

Two rules. Do not buy on credit, and do not name your weapon.

Water finding its way down. Stone settling. Under that, something turning over in its sleep, slowly, the way you turn when somebody else has got into the bed.
Wax burns on both wrists and smoke in your lungs. Your order calls that devotion. I call it Tuesday. Sit.

We got to the eleventh. Eleventh. Nobody believes it and I have stopped needing them to.
We left him on the sixth, where the roots come through the ceiling. His leg was broken and there was no getting him out. That is the whole story, and it takes nine seconds to tell.
Wenna Torr, surveyor. You are going down, so you can help. Count your steps on the stair. Count them again on the way up. Tell me both numbers.
What comes up from the Works holds an edge longer than anything I can make. It is quenched in something. I tried to find out what.

When the Third Expedition came home, three of them climbed the stair. I heard four sets of footsteps.

You will go. Everybody goes. When you get there, do not read the wall.

An army marched across these heights to take Caul from above, and the winter took the army instead. They are still up here, in their lines, in their camps, under the snow, facing the way they were facing. The weather has never let them go home.

Caul hanged its worst out here, over water, so the bodies would be somebody else's problem. The water took them politely and has been asking for more. The boardwalks are mended every night. Nobody has seen who mends them.

Caul ran out of room for its dead long before it ran out of dead, so it planted a wood over the overflow and called it a park. The roots went down and found what they were fed. The trees have been grateful ever since, in their way.

When the sand came, the city's kings went down into their tombs and had the doors sealed after them, to wait it out. They are still waiting. Their servants went in with them, and their soldiers, and they have all stayed loyal.

Caul paid for nine hundred years. Then it stopped paying, and went down to settle the account in person.

Corvane will enter it in the book under assets.

Go on. Down is the only direction that holds.
It has started leaving the lamps lit for you.
It is not hiding. It is making room.

Keep going. It is the only direction that holds.
Marrow will want a longer chisel.

No survey mark reaches this far. No city built here. The layers are out of order now: crypt opens onto spire, spire onto ash, as if the Tenant had taken its own history down off the shelf and put it back in a hurry.
Nothing on this tier was built. It was made room for.
Something has been counting since the Spire went in. The Archive guessed it was counting the dead. The tallies on these walls say otherwise. It counts delvers.
Somewhere on this tier a bell rings once, very far up, and you realise it is the camp's.
Stairhead exists to keep one delver on the stair. When nobody is down there, things come up. When somebody is, they go down to meet them. Nobody in camp will tell you which of those is the point.
That is all the Spire is for. It is a nail. It has been working loose for a thousand years, and the stair at Stairhead opened the year it moved.
The Cindergate Works were built to arm Caul against what lived under it. Their order books name no enemy. They give a depth.
The Hollow Spire did not grow. It was driven, point first, from somewhere the sky does not reach, and it went through every layer the cities built until it struck the Tenant and pinned it.
The Listener was right about the one thing she never said aloud. The deep does not sit still while you walk it. It rises to meet whoever is lowest, the way water finds the deepest cut.
The Listener, a very long way up, turns her ear from the floor for the first time in years and sleeps.

The Rime Archive kept a list. Caul fed it. The Works armed against it. The Sanctum prayed to it. The hive ate what it left. The Archive froze it. A country burned itself to starve it. Something from outside nailed it down.
